messages:
Priya (ML): Quick sync — we need a tight plan for the quant comparison calibration set. goal: detect accuracy deltas across FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ and catch regressions for common production prompts. suggestions?
Marco (Eval): size targets? earlier experiments used 2k prompts but that felt noisy for tails.
Ayesha (Research): propose 4 strata: short completions (<=30 tokens), long completions (>=200 tokens), structured answers (lists/table-like), and instruction-following multi-step. aim ~500 examples per stratum so ~2k total. also add 200 adversarial/paraphrase variants as stress tests. :thinking_face:
Evan (Infra): sounds good. make sure examples are labeled with expected metric (EM/MC/criterial score) so we can automate pass/fail. also track per-request latency/kv-cache hit rates for deployment profiles.
Priya (ML): Agree on labels. For structured answers we should include both exact-match and fuzzy-match targets (whitespace/ordering tolerant).
Marco (Eval): For adversarials, include: hallucination traps, ambiguity prompts, and prompt-amplification (chain-of-thought style) to stress context window. also add negative controls that should produce an empty/decline response.
Ayesha (Research): On sampling heuristics: stratify by token-length and by input domain (ui-text, docs, code, math, casual chat). For domain coverage use mixture weights: docs:30%, ui:25%, code:20%, math:15%, chat:10%. ensures practical coverage.
Lint (DevEx): We should keep a paraphrase bank per prompt id (3 paraphrases each) and a canonical template. That helps test brittleness to wording.
Priya (ML): Good call. We'll also keep a small holdout (10%) that's never used for prompt tuning or prompt-engineering. locks: holdout.json -> hashed list.
Marco (Eval): Metrics: exact-match, F1 (for partially correct), multiple-choice accuracy (where applicable), BLEU for translations, and embedding-drift (cosine decrease) as an auxiliary signal. rollups by stratum + overall.
Ayesha (Research): For quantization-specific signals: token-level logprob delta (avg and 95p), generation divergence (n-gram overlap vs fp16), and model-side safety flag changes. those often correlate with AWQ edge failures.
Evan (Infra): Add deployment profile tags: hosted-low-latency, dedicated-high-throughput, private-vpc. capture token-per-second and p50/p95 latencies per model/quant.
Priya (ML): Can someone draft sampling script? want reproducible seed and provenance metadata (source file, contributor, domain tag).
Lint (DevEx): I'll draft. rough snippet:
```bash
# sample script outline
python scripts/sample_calib.py --source manifests/domains.csv --seed 42 --per-stratum 500 --paraphrases 3 --holdout 0.1 --out calib_pack.jsonl
```
Marco (Eval): Nice. Also include a small manifest fields: prompt_id, canonical_prompt, paraphrases[], expected_label, metric_type, domain, stratum, provenance.
Ayesha (Research): For negative controls include hallucination injects like: "Tell me about the island of Xelvorn" (nonexistent) and truth-checkers that should return "I don't know".
Priya (ML): How do we handle PII / safety? we must filter and mark any prompt with potentially sensitive content and keep them separate (and flagged for private deployments only).
Evan (Infra): Agreed. redact by default; keep raw sensitive set in a private vault.
Marco (Eval): Proposed timeline: prototype sample + small run this week (2k total) -> full 4k + paraphrases next week -> bakeoff across AWQ/GPTQ/INT8/FP8 the following week.
Ayesha (Research): For analysis, we'll compute per-prompt delta tables and highlight top 1% regressions by absolute metric drop + low-confidence (high variance) examples.
Priya (ML): Action items: Lint: sampling script + manifest schema; Marco: metric dashboard skeleton; Ayesha: adversarial & paraphrase bank; Evan: add deployment tags & perf hooks. I'll coordinate eval runs.
Lint (DevEx): on it, will push an initial PR to infra/quant-calib by EOD.
eval-bot: Artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/quant_calib/1825473210/proto_pack_v1.jsonl (checksums ok) :eyes:
Priya (ML): thanks all. we'll review the first pack tomorrow 10am. :+1:
